📰 General

NFL Analyst Predicts Cowboys’ Rueben Bain Jr. Selection in 2026 Mock Draft •

A recent NFL mock draft, compiled by Mike Band, projects the Dallas Cowboys to select defensive end Reuben Bain Jr. with the first overall pick in 2026. The mock draft anticipates the Las Vegas Raiders will choose Heisman Trophy winner, bolstering the team’s existing quarterback situation. The Steelers and Philadelphia Eagles are also slated to select wide receivers within the top selections. This projection highlights anticipated trends in team needs and potential draft strategies for several NFL franchises.

🌍 World

Atlantic Current Collapse Now Far More Likely, New Research Reveals •

Recent research indicates a significantly higher probability of the Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation (AMOC) collapsing than previously estimated. Scientists utilizing updated climate models have determined these models accurately represent the current trajectory of the system’s decline. The research suggests the AMOC, responsible for regulating global temperatures, is approaching a critical tipping point. This collapse would have dramatic consequences, including colder temperatures in Europe and North America, and significant shifts in global weather patterns.

🦅 US

Pope Leo XIV Describes Algeria Visit as “Special Blessing” Promoting Dialogue •

Pope Leo XIV reflected on his recent Apostolic Journey to Algeria, describing the visit as a “special blessing” and an opportunity to foster dialogue. During a flight from Algiers to Yaoundé, the Pope shared his observations with the reporters traveling with him. He emphasized the importance of the trip in promoting understanding and communication within the diverse Algerian society. The journey focused on engaging with various communities and religious groups within the country.

💰 Business

FCC Grants Netgear Exemption from Router Ban, Lacking Explanation •

The Federal Communications Commission recently granted Netgear an exemption from the US government’s ban on foreign-made routers. This marks the first instance a major consumer router vendor has received such an exception. The exemption specifically applies to Netgear’s Nighthawk and Orbi router lines. The FCC’s decision has raised questions regarding the rationale behind the exemption and its potential implications for other companies. Details about the specific criteria used for this particular exemption remain undisclosed.

💻 Technology

Movement Gaining Traction: People Seek Freedom From Smartphone Dependence •

A group of millennials experimented with a “digital detox” session in Brooklyn, intentionally abstaining from smartphone use for two hours. The participants engaged in activities like reading and conversation to combat potential screen addiction. This initiative reflects a growing trend of individuals seeking to reduce their reliance on mobile devices and their associated distractions. The experiment highlights a rising concern about the impact of constant screen time on attention and social interaction.

🎭 Entertainment

Meghan Trainor Opens Up About Ashley Tisdale Drama, Reveals Texts Sent •

Meghan Trainor recently discussed the fallout from Ashley Tisdale’s essay detailing a group of mothers she described as “toxic.” Trainor revealed that Tisdale sent her direct messages following the essay’s publication, expressing her discomfort with the situation. The exchange reportedly involved Tisdale clarifying her intentions and explaining the context of her observations. Trainor stated that the messages were a significant part of her processing the experience. She described the interaction as a crucial step in understanding the dynamics of the group.

🏅 Sports

Senator Baldwin to Introduce Bill Promoting Accessibility in NFL Broadcasting •

Senator Tammy Baldwin (D-Wisc.) is set to introduce a bill focused on improving accessibility within the NFL’s broadcasting practices. The proposed legislation responds to ongoing criticism regarding the league’s approach to broadcasting and its handling of various challenges. Details regarding the specific provisions of the bill remain under wraps, but the intention is to address concerns raised about the NFL’s current broadcasting strategies. This move represents a significant step towards potentially reshaping the league’s broadcasting landscape.

🔬 Science

Subaru Telescope Reveals Dramatic Chemical Transformations in Interstellar Comet 3I/ATLAS •

Astronomers utilizing the Subaru Telescope have observed significant chemical changes occurring within Interstellar Comet 3I/ATLAS, a comet originating outside our solar system. The observations, made in December 2025, provide a unique opportunity to study the composition of comets from beyond our planetary system. Scientists identified evidence of volatile compounds, including carbon monoxide and methane, undergoing substantial alterations as the comet approached the Sun. These changes offer valuable data for understanding the processes involved in the formation of planets and planetesimals.

🩺 Health

CDC Issues Urgent Warning: Drug-Resistant Shigella Threatens US Public Health •

The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) has issued a warning regarding a rise in drug-resistant Shigella bacteria circulating across the United States. This strain of Shigella, responsible for causing Shigellosis, is spreading through contact with contaminated feces and is characterized by symptoms including explosive diarrhea and severe abdominal pain. Researchers are particularly concerned about the bacteria’s resistance to multiple antibiotics, complicating treatment efforts. The CDC is urging increased vigilance and public health measures to mitigate the potential spread of this emerging threat.
